    1. F1   INPUT accepts new connections to any port                                   +15, grade C

  Findings

  HIGH     F1   INPUT accepts new connections to any port                                        -15
                No rule refuses them, and the policy of filter/INPUT is ACCEPT. Every port that no
                rule names is open: a service that listens on one, now or later, is reachable at
                once.
                fix  Add rules for the traffic that is needed and test them, with a way back, then
                     set the policy to DROP. The recommended baseline (--baseline) is a complete
                     rule set to start from.
                     Deny by default (IPv4):
                       iptables -P INPUT DROP
                     Deny by default (IPv6):
                       ip6tables -P INPUT DROP

  HIGH     F2   5 services are open to any source because INPUT accepts by default               -14
                No rule names their ports: sshd on 22/tcp; nginx on 80/tcp (IPv4 only); nginx on
                443/tcp (IPv4 only); mysqld on 3306/tcp (IPv4 only); dhclient on 68/udp (IPv4 only).
                Close the default first; then accept each port that must stay reachable, for its
                clients only.

  HIGH     F3   All ports of the containers on bridge br-982052ef0162 are reachable by direct     -3
                routing (IPv4, possible)
                Every port of containers on bridge br-982052ef0162 (gateway mode nat-unprotected) is
                forwarded to hosts that route 172.29.0.2 via this host (for example on the same L2
                segment), including ports that were never published; neither INPUT nor
                published-port rules apply.
                fix  Use the default gateway mode "nat" for this network, or drop new non-DNAT
                     connections into the bridge in DOCKER-USER.
                     Drop packets for the containers that do not arrive from their bridge (published
                     ports keep working):
                       iptables -t raw -I PREROUTING -d 172.29.0.0/24 ! -i br-982052ef0162 -j DROP
                     Or refuse new connections into the bridge that no published port translated:
                       iptables -I DOCKER-USER -o br-982052ef0162 ! -i br-982052ef0162 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m conntrack ! --ctstate DNAT -j DROP

  MEDIUM   F4   6 Docker published ports are open to any source                                  -16
                Docker translates these ports to containers, and filter/FORWARD accepts them from
                any source; the rules of filter/INPUT do not apply: IPv4 8080/tcp to 172.17.0.2:80;
                IPv4 8082/tcp of 192.168.88.217 to 172.17.0.4:80; IPv4 9053/udp to 172.17.0.5:53;
                IPv4 9000-9002/tcp to 172.17.0.6:9000-9002; IPv4 8091/tcp to 172.29.0.2:80; IPv4
                8443/tcp to 172.30.0.2:443; IPv6 8443/tcp to [fd00:dead:beef::2]:443.
                fix  Docker translates published ports in nat/PREROUTING, so they are forwarded and
                     never reach filter/INPUT (this includes INPUT rules of ufw or firewalld).
                     Restrict them in DOCKER-USER, which runs before Docker's own rules and which
                     Docker never flushes. Packets are already translated there: match the published
                     port with --ctorigdstport, not --dport. A service that only local clients need
                     can be published on loopback instead (docker run -p
                     127.0.0.1:8080:<container-port>). The commands below are for port 8080/tcp. For
                     each of the other ports (8082/tcp of 192.168.88.217, 9053/udp, 9000-9002/tcp,
                     8091/tcp, 8443/tcp), run them again with its protocol and its port; write a
                     range of ports as FIRST:LAST. For a port of one address, add --ctorigdst
                     ADDRESS; for a port of all addresses, leave that match out. For IPv6, use
                     ip6tables.
                     Allow the trusted sources of port 8080 first:
                       iptables -I DOCKER-USER 1 -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8080 --ctdir ORIGINAL -s <trusted-cidr> -j RETURN
                     Then drop the rest of that port:
                       iptables -I DOCKER-USER 2 -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8080 --ctdir ORIGINAL -j DROP

  MEDIUM   F5   Container port 172.31.0.2:80 is reachable by direct routing (IPv4, possible)      -1
                Container port 172.31.0.2:80/tcp on bridge br-84b7b034b576 (gateway mode routed) is
                forwarded without NAT to hosts that route 172.31.0.2 via this host (for example on
                the same L2 segment); host INPUT rules do not apply to it.
                fix  Restrict the container port in DOCKER-USER (match -d 172.31.0.2 --dport 80), or
                     use gateway mode nat.
                     Drop the container port for all but the trusted sources:
                       iptables -I DOCKER-USER -o br-84b7b034b576 -d 172.31.0.2 -p tcp --dport 80 ! -s <trusted-cidr> -j DROP

    udp  68 dhclient (IPv4 only) · all ports that no rule names
